Brief facts of the case 1.

The Final Report u/s 173 Cr. PC runs to the effect that on 05.05.2018, it was telephonically informed by the caller Sh. Pritam that his daughter (married) had committed suicide by hanging herself and that she had also left a suicide note.
This information was reduced into writing as DD No.40B which was entrusted to SI Begraj.

The said police official reached at the spot i.e. H.No. D 594, Gali No.5, Ashok Nagar, Delhi and on inquiry found that the victim (deceased Madhu) had already been taken to GTB Hospital where she was declared brought dead by the doctor and that deceased had also tried to strangulate her son, but somehow he survived.

Crime Team was called at the spot, who snapped photographs of the SOC wherefrom a suicide note was recovered and taken into police FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No.
2 of 18 possession.
Inquiry revealed that the unnatural death had taken place within seven years of marriage and accordingly the SDM of the area was informed.

Police lodged the present case FIR on State vs Amit Kumar on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29099736/
1 the statement (made to the SDM) of Sh. Pritam Singh (father).
In the said statement (dated 05.05.2018) he apprised that the marriage of his daughter Madhubala (since deceased) had been solemnized as on 02.12.2015 with Amit Kumar s/o Sh. Rambir.
Said Sh. Rambir used to do a private job.

At about 11.48 a.m, Complainant Sh. Pritam Singh received a message from his daughter Madhu on his mobile phone No.9350167564 to the effect that "Papa mai jaa rahi hoon, app sabse bahut door, ye sab log bahut bure hai, mera jeena haram kiya hua hai in logon ne meri saas mera sasur bahut ganda ganda bolte hai mujhe suna nahi jaata ye sab, papa maine eak note likha hai jo mere room mei eak micky mouse rakha hai ussi mei wo note bhi rakha hai ".
Immediately on receiving this message, Complainant Pritam Singh dialed 100 number and apprised to the police about the same.
The father in law of his deceased daughter was also informed in that regard.
FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 3 of 18 2.
Further, the Complaint also runs to the effect that just 3-4 months of the marriage of his daughter, her mother in law, father in law and husband had started harassing her.
A WagonR car had also been given in dowry for which, they were demanding cash in lieu thereof.
It is further alleged therein that due to their harassment, Madhu committed suicide.
3. After completion of the investigation, police filed the Charge Sheet in the due course against four persons i.e. parents -in-law, husband and sister-in-law namely Kavita.

4. Vide Order on Charge dated 05.04.2019, accused Kavita (sister-in-law) stood discharged whereas the charges u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC were ordered to be framed as against the remaining three accused persons i.e. parents-in-law and the husband.
(The discharge order qua one of the accused namely Kavita was also affirmed by the Hon'ble High Court vide order dated 18.01.2023).
The Charges were framed on the very day i.e. 05.04.2019 to which all the three accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 4 of 18 5.
Prosecution examined 13 witnesses in support of the case and the PE stood closed as on 25.07.2024.

SA u/s 313 Cr. P.C was recorded as on 05.08.2024 wherein they opted to lead DE and examined Sh. Ravinder Kumar as DW1 and Sh. Devender Kumar as DW2 (both neighbours) and the DE stood closed vide order dated 10.09.2024.
Prosecution Witnesses PW-1 Ct. Mukesh - He was member of the Mobile Crime Team who had tried to lift chance prints from the spot, but no such chance prints could be recovered/lifted.

PW-2 HC Pawan- He is a witness of record in the capacity of being posted as MHC(M) who produced requisite registers (No. 19 & 21) to prove the relevant entries vide which, the case properties were deposited in the maalkhana.

2 PW-3 Sh. Pritam Singh - He is the Complainant/father of the deceased on whose behest the proceedings were initiated.
PW-4 Smt. Vijay Laxmi - She happens to be the mother of the deceased.
PW-5 Sh. Munni Lal - He is a neighbour of the Complainant, who was witness to the marriage FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 5 of 18 ceremony of the deceased
and has also deposed about the alleged cruel treatment for/in connection with the demand of money in lieu of the returned dowry articles i.e. the WagonR car.

PW-6 SI Suman Kumar - He was the incharge of the Mobile Crime Team in whose presence certain part of the investigation was conducted at the spot including the recovery of handwritten suicide note kept in a micky mouse like toy and also witnessed some writing on the wall in the form of a suicide note.
PW-7 ASI Ram Snehi - He had performed the duty as Duty Officer on 05.05.2018.
PW-8 HC Mahavir Singh - He was member of the Mobile Crime Team as Photographer who had snapped 24 photographs at the spot as on 05.05.2018.
PW-9 Sh. Pramod - He is the brother of the deceased.
PW-10 ASI Begraj Singh - He is the 1st IO of the case.
PW-11 SI Shikshit Kumar - This police official had joined the investigation with the main IO/Inspector Jai Bhagwan.
PW-12 ASI Roop Kumar - This police official had accompanied the 1st IO/ASI Begraj to the spot as on 05.05.2018.
FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 6 of 18 PW-13 Inspector Jai Bhagwan- He is the IO of the case who filed the Charge Sheet after completion of the investigation.
6. File perused.
Ld. Defence Counsel as well as Ld. Addl. PP heard.
7. Since the accused persons have been Charged with for the offences u/s 304B/498A/34 IPC, the prosecution is required to satisfy the ingredients thereof.

8. For the offence u/s 304B IPC, the ingredients are :-
 i). Death of a (married) women within 07  years of her marriage.
ii). Death is caused by burns/bodily injuries or otherwise than under normal circumstances.

State vs Amit Kumar on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29099736/
3 iii).
Soon before her death, she was subjected to cruelty/harassment by her husband/any relative of husband and iv).
the aforesaid ill treatment was for/in connection with any demand of dowry.

9. For the offence u/s 498A, it is required to be proved that the husband or relative of husband (of such women) subjected her to cruelty as explained in sub-clauses (a) and (b) of the Explanation appended therewith.
FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 7 of 18 Appreciation of Material on Record Day of Death & its cause 10.
As per the prosecution version, the victim Madhubala allegedly committed suicide on 05.05.2018 by hanging herself at the house of her in laws in the forenoon.
(Her marriage had been solemnized with accused No.1 Amit Kumar on 02.12.2015).
She was taken to GTB hospital by her husband Amit as reflected in her MLC Ex. P-1.

This MLC reveals that she was brought to hospital in unconscious and unresponsive state with the alleged history of hanging at about 12.00 noon on the very day i.e. 05.05.2018 as apprised by her husband.

She was declared dead around 12.40 p.m (i.e.
at the time of her examination itself).

Her postmortem was conducted on the next day i.e.
06.05.2018 vide PMR No. 764/18 (Ex. P-2).
In the 'Opinion' part thereof, the cause of death is shown as "Asphyxia as a result of antemortem hanging".
The viscera was got preserved and its examination report (FSL Rohini dated 30.11.2018) rules out any sort of poison in the exhibits sent for analysis.
Thus, neither it is alleged nor otherwise there is any such thing suggestive of homicidal death
and in defence also, this aspect (suicide) has not at all been FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 8 of 18 disputed even to the slightest extent.

sentences.text: Hence, it can very well be concluded that the death of Madhubala took place as on 05.05.2018 around 12.00 noon by way of suicide by hanging at the in laws house.
Thus, it was an 'unnatural death' which took place within a period of less than 03 years reckoned from the date of marriage.
Death - Whether a Dowry Death or not 11.
Admittedly, there is no controversy at all w.r.t the first two ingredients of the offence u/s 304B IPC as reflected here-in- above.

However, it is yet to be seen (by appreciation of the evidence)
whether the prosecution has been successful in proving the rest two ingredients thereof.

12. In this context, testimony of her family members i.e. parents and brother (PW3, PW4 and PW9),
testimony of a family friend (PW5) and the documentary evidence (particularly the handwritten suicide note Ex. P4 ) are to be looked into.
FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc.
Pg. No. 9 of 18 13.

Sh. Pritam Singh (PW3; father of the deceased) had got recorded his statement Ex. PW3/A as on 05.05.2018 itself wherein it is reflected that at about 11.48 a.m, he had received a message on his mobile phone No. 9350167564 from his daughter to the effect that 'Papa mai jaa rahi hoon aap sabse bahut door, ye sab log bahut bure hai, mera jeena haram kiya hua in logon ne, meri saas, mera sasur bahut ganda ganda bolte had, mujhse nahi suna jaata ye sab, Papa maine eak note likha hai, jo mere State vs Amit Kumar on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29099736/
4 room mei eak micky mouse rakha hai, ussi mei woh note bhi rakha hai'.
It is also reflected in the said statement that immediately after reading this message of his daughter, he dialed 100 number and apprised the police of the same.
Thus, the next document to be looked into is the DD No. 40B dated 05.05.2018 vide which, the 100 number call made by PW3 was reduced into writing.
This document stands proved on record as Ex. PW10/C vide the testimony of ASI Begraj Singh.

A bare perusal of Ex. PW10/C makes it ample clear that the ' caller ' (i.e. PW3 Sh. Pritam Singh) had duly apprised the police about having received a message on his mobile phone from his daughter (since deceased) and in this regard, the reflection made in the statement FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 10 of 18 Ex. PW3/A is on the right footing.

PW3 even produced his mobile phone during the course of his examination in chief conducted on 18.07.2019 on the basis of which, the 'Text Message' was verbatim brought on record which further substantiates the prosecution version in general and the veracity of the Complainant's assertion in particular as appearing in the statement/Complaint Ex. PW3/A (at least) in this context.
14. Proceeding ahead in the same sequence; the next aspect is that of the recovery of the alleged suicide note in terms of the text message made by the victim and as revealed by the Complainant.
The said suicide note has been made part of the proceedings and is shown exhibited as Ex. P-4.
As per PW3 Sh. Pritam Singh, the mickey mouse (toy) containing the handwritten suicide note was recovered from the house of in laws of her deceased daughter.
The recovery of the mickey mouse stands established on record vide memo Ex. PW3/B and that of the suicide note vide seizure memo Ex. PW3/E.
This witness (i.e. PW3) has also duly deposed that both these seizure memos do bear his signatures thereon.

The recovery aspect was not at all FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg.
No. 11 of 18 agitated during his cross examination.
Further, it also stands duly proved vide the testimony of PW3 and PW4 (parents of the deceased) that the said suicide note was in the handwriting of their daughter Madhubala.
Otherwise also, it is an undisputed fact as there are not suggestions at all nugatory to the afore- assertion(s).

It would not be out of context to mention herein that even the FSL Report dated 31.07.2018 vide which, the handwriting of the suicide note was compared with the admitted writings (i.e. a practical book containing the handwriting of the deceased daughter of PW3) affirmed the fact that the suicide note was in the handwriting of the deceased Madhubala.

The opinion reflected in the FSL report dated 31.07.2018 is to the effect that :-
"the person who wrote blue enclosed admitted writings stamped and marked A1 to A156 also wrote red enclosed question writings similarly stamped and marked Q1 &
Q2........"
15.

It is also reflected in the very report (in the reasons explained in detail) that similarities were also observed in the 'admitted writings' and the 'questioned writings' without there FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 12 of 18 being any fundamental divergence therein and hence, those similarities in writing habits were significant and sufficient and were not attributable to accidental co-incidence and this way the afore-quoted opinion/conclusion was arrived at by the Expert.
16.
Now looking into the very contents of the handwritten suicide note, it is to be ascertained whether it reflects any sort of cruelty/harassment which ultimately led the victim to commit suicide.
Its very language does contain allegations against the parents-in-law as well as her husband.

sentences.text: very starting line thereof is to the effect that it were her parents-in-law and her husband responsible for her death.
The use of abusive language is attributed to them mainly for the reason of demand/greed of money.
This aspect has also been substantiated vide the respective testimonies of the family members of deceased.
To be more precise, both the parents (PW3 & PW4) have duly raised the allegations to the effect that they had given the dowry articles including one WagonR car at the time of marriage.

The said WagonR car was returned back by the in laws and they started demanding money in lieu thereof which was beyond their FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc.
Pg. No. 13 of 18 capacity to pay as the car had been got financed and the said liability was still being discharged in monthly installments.
On this aspect, there are strange suggestions put to these witnesses.
For example, during the cross examination of PW3, it was suggested that 'except the WagonR car and cash in lieu thereof no other demand was ever made by the accused '.
This suggestion; though was answered in affirmative by the witness, yet is itself a sufficient evidence of the demand of dowry.

Same is the fate of cross examination of PW4 and the relevant portion thereof is being reproduced hereunder:-
"accused persons only used to demand the money in lieu of the price of the car and nothing else".

17. Thus the cumulative effect of all these material aspects is that the accused persons had been harassing/ill treating the victim and the said ill treatment was in connection with the demand of dowry (WagonR car/ money in lieu thereof).
FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 14 of 18 18.

"Soon before death" is the next aspect to be looked into and for that purpose, the date/timing of the suicide note as well as the whatsapp/text message of the fateful day is/are the relevant material.
Date/Timing of the Suicide Note 19.
The recovery of the suicide note and the same being in the handwriting of deceased have already been proved as above.
However, a bare perusal of the suicide note makes it clear that there is 'cutting' over it at the place where the date was mentioned over it at the end.
However, despite cutting over the date, it can still be deciphered as '12.4.2018', meaning thereby that it might have been written at least 02 weeks prior to committing suicide on 05.05.2018.
The date of the suicide note stands further affirmed by way of the testimony of PW3 Sh. Pritam Singh in its cross examination conducted as on 31.07.2019.

This cross examination when read in the light of the very narration of the suicide note Ex. P4, affirms the aspect that some sort of scolding had taken place in the morning of 20.04.2018, when the victim had returned on the said day after FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 15 of 18 attending the marriage of her friend Richa (marriage date 19.04.2018) and it (scolding) started on account of her getting up late in the morning.
Thus, it becomes clear that even after reducing the suicide note into writing, the victim gave it a second thought instead of committing suicide immediately.
However, apparently, there was no change in the environment/treatment meted out to the victim as is reflected in the duly proved whatsapp/text message (dated 05.05.2018).

6
Appreciation for the purpose u/s 498A IPC 20.
The afore-findings also well cover the requirements u/s 498A IPC.

The oral testimony of the prosecution witnesses; particularly that of her family members, the documentary evidence in the form of the suicide note and the text message is/are clear enough to conclude that the victim was being subjected to cruelty and the cruel treatment was within the meaning of the Explanation appended therewith in its requirements under sub clause (a) & (b).
FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 16 of 18 The defence at a glance 21.

entities.text: State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 16 of 18
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Besides cross examining the prosecution witnesses, two witnesses/neighbours have also been examined as defence witnesses.

The defence as appearing therein (coupled with the crux of the cross examination of PWs as well as the SA u/s 313 Cr. P.C) is to the effect that it were the family members of the deceased herself who were in the habit of visiting her at her in laws house and quarreling with her and that she had some sort of mental problem/suicidal tendency.
As far as the defence of there being any mental problem with the deceased is concerned, it is entirely a vague assertion as nothing such could be brought on record in any sense.

In respect of the second aspect i.e. visits paid by the parents/family members of the deceased at her in laws house, this defence was introduced in the deposition of the defence witnesses who are residents of the same gali/neighbours of the accused persons.
Apparently there was no reason for them of coming to know about any such alleged visits paid at the house of accused persons.
Moreover, no such suggestion was put either to the parents or to the brother of the deceased when they were examined as prosecution witnesses.

Thus, apparently and FIR No. 150/18 State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 17 of 18 clearly, the defence on these lines is an afterthought version and this way, there is no substance at all in the evidence so led.

entities.text: State Vs. Amit Kumar Etc. Pg. No. 17 of 18
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Conclusion 22. The appreciation made here-in-above makes it ample clear that the prosecution has successfully proved its case beyond reasonable doubts.
The ingredients of the offences u/s 304B and 498A IPC have duly been established.

All the accused persons are thus found and held guilty for the offence(s)
with which they were Charged for and are convicted accordingly.
Announced in Open Court on 07th February 2025 (RAGHUBIR SINGH)
